correctness.rationale: For fixed m0>=3, rates beta,lambda>0 and a walker jumping to any other vertex uniformly, the exact lumped process (A=N-1,D=X-1) has birth rate beta and discovery intensity lambda(A-D)/A. With alpha=lambda/(lambda+beta), R=D-alpha A has drift -lambda R/A. Its compensated birth/discovery martingales have limiting quadratic brackets beta t and a t, a=beta*lambda/(beta+lambda), and zero cross-variation. A second-moment estimate bounds R_t^2 by O(t); the cutoff epsilon argument justifies convergence to the stochastic entrance integral of s^k dW with k=lambda/beta, even at small positive k. Itô isometry gives covariance [[beta,beta*k^2/(1+k)^2],[same,beta*k*(k^2+1)/(1+k)^3]]. Checked exact algebra and frozen verify.py finite-step rational lumping/generator code. Independent simulation at t=300, beta=lambda=1, 4500 trials yielded approximate per-time variance/covariance (1.001,0.251,0.250), versus theoretical (1,0.25,0.25); simulation does not prove convergence.
